rules.rule: Initial capture and sustained attention are separate mechanisms; strong early capture does not imply sustained processing.
Expected information gain is an anticipated knowledge update; epistemic value is the subjective worth assigned to obtaining information.
A learning-progress signal is a subjective/computational mechanism, not simply the fact that performance improved.
Appraisals jointly differentiate emotions; no one appraisal is a direct emotion label.
Group prototypicality is fit to a salient group prototype; perceived similarity/homophily is broader interpersonal or audience-source similarity.
Perceived genuineness/authenticity can contribute to credibility/trust but is not identical to trustworthiness.
Parasocial intimacy is relational; creator familiarity can arise from repeated exposure without intimacy.
Privacy cost concerns unwanted information exposure/control; reputational risk concerns social evaluation/image consequences.
Practical/information-value motives cannot be inferred solely from an observed share.
Goal-directed action-outcome control and context-response/habitual control can coexist and compete.
Do not make a discrete central arbiter mandatory; arbitration is one model among alternatives including dynamic integration.
